messages:
rebecca: Heads-up: small base-image rebuild planned Tue 07:45 PT. Objectives: drop CAP_NET_RAW and CAP_SYS_ADMIN where we can, enforce seccomp/runtime/default, and migrate keystore operator to per-cluster KMS aliases.

mitchel: Sounds good. Are we doing a rolling canary or a hard flip?

rebecca: Rolling canary: dev-canary -> perf -> prod-canary -> rest. 10m windows, automated health checks. Also will rotate cosign signer during the pipeline.

yasmin: RBAC cleanup is required before any promote. bake-runner SA still has broad bindings in a few namespaces. I'll open a migration PR to tighten perms and add an audit annotation for SOC tracking.

mitchel: For the KMS plan: per-cluster alias makes revocation safer. Who provisions the aliases and grants keystore-operator access?

rebecca: infra will create aliases like projects/redwood/keys/keystore-<cluster>.mitchel, can you own the grant step? Need kms:Encrypt/kms:Decrypt plus iam.serviceAccounts.actAs for the operator.

oncall-bot: ticket SEC-9001 created: base-image rebuild + keystore per-cluster keys + cosign rotation.

yasmin: Audit/retention question: SOC wants immutable access for 1 year. If logs are encrypted with cluster KEK, how do we ensure immutability and prove provenance?

rebecca: Plan: write audit batches to a WORM bucket and attach a signed manifest (cosign) for each upload. Logs encrypted with cluster KEK; manifest proves which images/keys were used. I'll attach schema to SEC-9001.

mitchel: Build pipeline change: add SBOM (cyclonedx), cosign attestations, and a reproducible-build flag. Also enforce `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` in Docker build to reduce nondeterminism.

yasmin: Incident runbook item: if keystore rewrap fails mid-rollout, fallback is to decrypt with the previous KEK and rewrap. Need explicit commands and controlled escalation path. I'll author the runbook and include a short-lived impersonation token example.

rebecca: Example precheck for rollout team:
```
# verify no NET_RAW in running pods
kubectl get pods -o jsonpath='{.items[*].spec.containers[*].securityContext.capabilities.drop}' | grep NET_RAW && echo BAD || echo OK
# cosign verify for the promoted tag
cosign verify --bundle -key k8s://projects/redwood/keys/cosign registry/redwood/base:sha
# check seccomp profile
kubectl get pod -o jsonpath='{.items[*].spec.containers[*].securityContext.seccompProfile}' | grep runtime/default || echo MISSING
```

mitchel: RBAC PR must include an annotation like `sec.redwood/audit=SEC-9001` on Roles/Bindings. SOC will use that to correlate changes.

yasmin: Monitoring: add alerts to trigger incident if >5 rewrap errors in 10m or if cosign verify fails post-promotion. That should auto-open an incident and attach to SEC-9001.

oncall-bot: deploy-checklist: [ ] RBAC PR merged (annotated), [ ] KMS aliases provisioned, [ ] cosign signer rotated and tested, [ ] SBOM + attestation pipeline green, [ ] canary schedule, [ ] runbook attached to SEC-9001.

rebecca: I'll post a 30m heads-up in #release-war-room before starting and monitor canary metrics. tagging owners: RBAC/yasmin, KMS/mitchel, signing/rebecca, runbook/yasmin. :mag:
